items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: But with Dion, I never knew that. The first six records we made with him were like million sellers.

ctx.x: Yeah. At the time did you ever have a sense of, well that song we did today, I think that is probably going to catch on?

No. Well once in a while I would say well there’s a hit record you know. And sure enough it would be a hit. But with Dion, I never knew that. The first six records we made with him were like million sellers. “The Wanderer” and “Teenager in Love.” But when I was with Vaughn Monroe we made a recording of a tune called “Riders in the Sky.” It was a different kind of rhythm. It was [scats] with the guitars. It was made in Chicago. And when we played a one-nighter in Detroit a few days later Vaughn played it about…
You never quite know what’s going to catch the public’s ear.

items.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015
items.q: And Dion would come and dictate what he wanted us to do.

ctx.x: Who hires you for this kind of thing?
The company. What was the name of the record company. Anyway they say that’s what we want. And Dion would come and dictate what he wanted us to do.

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: The first six records with Dion and the Belmonts I had Mundell Lowe was on guitar

ctx.x: Just that little lick that you were singing reminds me of a Paul Anka song. You did those things.
Oh yeah, we made a lot of those. I made all records. The first six records with Dion and the Belmonts I had Mundell Lowe was on guitar, George Barnes, all jazz guys on those rock & roll records.
